tldr: Finite-order experimental quantile precision depends on the realized empirical rank as well as the allocation fraction. The discovery note derives a uniform Gamma risk kernel for iid potential-outcome pairs under independently chosen main counts and completes the allocation space with exact and one-sided rank modes. This completed space characterizes every attainable limiting risk and gives a matching design lower bound for the stipulated left empirical QTE. A necessary-and-sufficient exact-balance result yields a strict fixed-count advantage on a nondegenerate amplitude region, while asymmetric amplitudes can favor a nonexact interior mode. The note supplies constructive global value certificates and envelope-only independent-pilot oracle attainment, with proof validation and Lean formalization tracked separately. The experimental criterion averages iid sampling and randomization.
gap: Zhang (2018), Theorem 4.1, is governed by Assumption 9, the unique-minimizer condition; supplement Lemma G.6 gives a separate sufficient condition that excludes integer effective ranks at constant propensity. Li, Luo, Wang and Feng (2025) is the closest optimal-QTE-allocation comparison candidate; its exact theorem scope remains externally unverifiable. Regular-quantile variance optimization does not by itself certify this finite-order bounded-risk objective.
fill: A labeled compact allocation space, a uniform conditional risk reduction, a complete attainable-risk frontier, exact-count stability on a legal open amplitude region, and concrete global-certification and pilot-learning questions make the design choice precise. Publication-level novelty remains conditional on completing the Li et al. comparison and the full proof obligations.
